dialog.body: Public Works, this is Lorraine, how can I help you this afternoon?

Hi, yeah, Lorraine. My name's Lucille Lombardozzi. I'm calling about the storm drain on our corner, and I'm gonna be honest, I wrote it all down because I'm sick of calling and forgetting half of it. So bear with me.
Take your time. What's the address?
Three Wellington Avenue. Down by the corner there, Fifth Ward. I rent the upstairs apartment. The owners live downstairs, Edson and Wilson Lopes.
Okay, 3 Wellington Avenue, upstairs apartment, owners are Lopes. And this is about the drain at the corner.

Yes. Okay, so, um. [pause] Hold on, I flipped the page. Okay. 'Friday night into Saturday, the storm, the drain at the corner backed up completely.' The water on the street was ankle deep. Ankle deep, Lorraine. I went out to move my car and it was over my sneakers. And people were still driving through it like nothing, throwing wakes right up onto the sidewalk and up the driveway. Like boats.
So during the storm that ended Saturday, the corner drain backed up, water ankle deep in the street, and cars going through it were pushing the water up toward the house.
Right. And the basement downstairs flooded. I don't use the basement, that's the Lopes', but Edson told me there was about three inches down there. They had to drag stuff out, it was a whole thing.
About three inches in the basement. Okay.

And here's the part that gets me. Wilson called you guys on Sunday. Sunday morning. And somebody told him a crew would come check the corner Monday. And a crew did come Monday, I'll give you that, I saw the truck. But all they did was clear off the grate and shovel the gunk out from around the top of it. That's it. Like twenty minutes and gone.

Let me pull it up. [pause] Okay, I do see it. Call came in Sunday the 11th from Wilson Lopes, drain backup at the corner, and there's a note the crew was out Monday the 12th. It says they cleared the grate and removed silt around the catch basin.

Around the top. Yeah. And it's still backing up. That's what I'm telling you. It's not fixed. There's still a puddle sitting there right now, three days after the storm stopped, and when anybody runs water or it drizzles at all it comes right back up. Whatever's wrong is under the street, not on top of it. Who actually looks under the street? Because the guy with the shovel isn't it.
So the grate's clear but the drain itself is still not taking the water, and you're still seeing it pool up at the corner today.

Today. Yes. And okay, hold on, there was another thing. [pause] Where'd I... okay. 'Neighbor.' The lady next door, she told me yesterday she called about the same drain too. Same corner, same mess. So my question is, are these all getting put together? Or is every call its own little ticket and somebody comes out and cleans the grate three separate times?

That's a fair question. I'm searching by the location now, not just your address. [pause] I see Wilson's call on there. I'm not finding another one under that corner right this second, but if she called under her own address it may be filed under that. What I'll do is put a note on this one that a neighbor reported the same drain, so whoever picks it up knows it's more than one house.
See, that's what I mean. Nobody's connecting anything. She called, Wilson called, now I'm calling. It's the same hole in the ground.
I hear you. I'm linking it to the existing report so it's all in one place, and I'm adding today's info, that it's still backing up after the crew was there Monday.

Okay. Good. Because honestly, I'm out every morning at like seven. I do deliveries, my first drop is the cafeteria at the school, and the school day starts at eight, so I'm racing the clock as it is. And I can't even pull straight out, I gotta go around the block because I'm not driving through that and soaking my brakes or splashing the kids waiting on the sidewalk. Every single morning. And it was supposed to be fixed Monday.
So it's affecting getting in and out of the street in the mornings too. I'll put that in.
Okay. Last thing on my list. [pause] Okay. 'Supervisor.' I want a supervisor to call me back. Not a crew, not another grate cleaning. Somebody who can actually decide to look at the pipe.
I can flag it for a supervisor to take a look at the drain and give you a call back. Let me get a good number for you.
401-555-0180. And that's Lucille, L-U-C-I-L-L-E?
Yup. Last name's Lombardozzi, L-O-M-B-A-R-D-O-Z-Z-I.

L-O-M-B-A-R-D-O-Z-Z-I. Got it. Okay, so let me read this back so you know what's going on the record. Corner drain at 3 Wellington Avenue. During the storm that ended Saturday it backed up, water ankle deep in the street, passing cars pushing it toward the house, and the basement downstairs took about three inches. Wilson Lopes reported it Sunday. Crew came Monday and cleared the grate and the silt on top. As of today, Tuesday, it's still backing up and holding water. A neighbor reported the same drain. You're requesting a supervisor look at it and call you back on your cell.
Yeah. That's it. That's everything on my paper.
Okay. I've flagged it for a supervisor.
And when's that gonna be? Like, are they coming out this week, or?

I don't have a new crew date on here yet. That's what the supervisor would decide once they look at it. After that storm we've got a lot of these going around town, so it may be a few days before you hear, but it's flagged as still not working, which moves it differently than a brand new call.
A few days. Okay. And if it rains again before then? Because it's January, it's gonna rain again, or snow, and then it's the same thing all over.

If it starts backing up again, call us right away and reference this report, and it'll go right on top of what's already there. And if you see water coming up the street at night, the after-hours line still takes drain calls.
I just feel like I'm doing your job for you, honestly. I wrote a whole page. Wilson already told you all this Sunday.

I know, and I'm sorry it's taking more than one call. Having it all written out actually helps, because now the note says plainly that the grate cleaning didn't solve it. That's what gets someone to look past the top of it.
Okay. Well. I'm gonna tell Wilson I called. He might call too, just so you know, he's like that.
That's fine, it'll all land on the same report now.
Alright. Thank you, Lorraine. I gotta get back in the truck.
Okay, Lucille. Drive safe.
